author: DamiLee
description:
The first time I rode the Central–Mid-Levels escalator, I didn't realize it only runs one way at a time: downhill from 6 to 10AM for the morning commute, then uphill until midnight. It's a chain of 20 escalators and three walkways, climbing 135 metres over 800 metres.

A few years after it opened in 1993, the government's auditor called it a "white elephant" because the cost had more than doubled. It didn't get drivers out of their cars either. But all that foot traffic quietly built SoHo ("South of Hollywood Road") as bars and restaurants opened along the route to catch the people riding past.

During its busiest hours, would you take the escalator or opt for the stairs?

title: Why Hong Kong Has the Longest Outdoor Escalator System
